title: Peddi Just Crossed ₹233 Crore in Four Days. Ram Charan Doesn't Do Comebacks.
excerpt: Three milestones, a $3 million North America weekend, and the definitive answer to everyone who wrote off the Mega Power Star after Game Changer.
body:
Four days. ₹233 crore worldwide. And a message, delivered in the only language Tollywood's box office understands: numbers that don't lie.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=noatJVfA22U

Ram Charan's Peddi crossed the ₹200 crore worldwide mark on Sunday — his third film to do so after RRR and Rangasthalam. For perspective, Game Changer, the film that was supposed to cement his post-RRR stardom, spent its entire theatrical run crawling to ₹185 crore. Peddi passed that number on Day 3. It didn't even slow down to notice.

The Weekend in Numbers

Directed by Buchi Babu Sana (the man behind Uppena), Peddi opened with a ₹51 crore India net on Day 1 — the second-biggest opening of Ram Charan's career, behind only RRR. The worldwide gross on opening day alone crossed ₹110 crore.

The pattern since then has been textbook front-loaded blockbuster with a twist: it's actually holding.

| Day | India Net | Worldwide Gross | |---|---|---| | Day 1 (Wed) | ₹51.00 Cr | ₹110+ Cr | | Day 2 (Thu) | ₹26.90 Cr | — | | Day 3 (Sat) | ₹28.85 Cr | ₹191 Cr (cumulative) | | Day 4 (Sun) | ₹31.90 Cr | ₹233 Cr (cumulative) |

The Sunday uptick — a 10.6% rise over Saturday — is the number that matters. It means families are showing up now, not just the first-day-first-show crowd. With 9,000+ shows still running across India, Peddi is holding screens in a month where nine major Bollywood releases are fighting for every seat.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZDwR_yzWbs/

North America: The Mega Family's Clean Sweep

Here's where it gets interesting for the diaspora. Peddi crossed $3 million in North America in just four days, surpassing the lifetime totals of Guntur Kaaram, Sye Raa, and Pushpa in 72 hours. It now sits alongside OG and MSVP as the only Telugu films to enter the $3 million club in the last 18 months — all three from the Mega Family.

Ram Charan's pull in North America has always been strong, but Peddi is proving it's not just dialled-in fans buying tickets. The sports-action premise, the family drama at its core, and the visceral mass moments are crossing the Telugu-speaking audience boundary. BookMyShow has the film in its Top 5 All-Time First Weekend Openers — a list dominated by pan-India juggernauts.

The Comeback Nobody Wants to Call a Comeback

Let's be honest about what happened. Game Changer was a disappointment — a bloated political drama that wasted Ram Charan's physicality and Shankar's reputation. It made money, but it didn't make believers. The whispers were loud: Was RRR a Rajamouli miracle? Can Ram Charan carry a film on his own name?

Peddi answers both questions in its opening weekend. Buchi Babu Sana has built a sports action drama that lets Ram Charan do what he does best — be intensely, overwhelmingly physical while carrying genuine emotional weight. Shiva Rajkumar, Jagapathi Babu, Divyenndu Sharma, and Boman Irani round out a cast that gives the film depth beyond its action set pieces.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DYzTGSds6wD/

What Happens Next

The immediate target is ₹300 crore worldwide, which looks comfortable if weekday holds stay above ₹10-12 crore net daily. The bigger question is whether Peddi can cross Rangasthalam's ₹212 crore to become Ram Charan's second-highest grosser ever. At this pace, that could happen by Wednesday.

For NRI audiences, the film is playing in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, and Hindi across most major markets. The Hindi version has been the softer performer — Telugu states remain the primary engine — but the international numbers suggest the film's appeal travels regardless of language.

Ram Charan doesn't do comebacks. He does demolitions. And Peddi just levelled everything that came before it.
